sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Pijao language' and (es) 'Idioma pijao', raw wikitext fetched sources 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing; word lists (after Loukotka 1963 / Ramírez Sendoya 1952) and pointers to Pineda Giraldo & Chaves 1943 ms., Reichel-Dolmatoff 1944, Durbin & Seijas 1973.

sources.citation: Zwisler, Joshua James. 2018. The Pijao of Natagaima: Post-Linguicide Indigenous Identity and Language. Cadernos de Etnolingüística 6(1): 51-80.
sources.note: §4.3 (pp. 70-72) gives a community-compiled Pijao word list in an orthography 'based on, but not identical, to the system used by Durbin and Seijas (1973) with diacritics representing stress' — stress is marked per item (amé, alamán, çaguála, golúpa, kahírre, hoté, huíl, nuhúgi, tínki, toléma, tenú, óreme...) but no rule is stated. §4.2 describes the Spanish ethnolect of Natagaima (word-final vowel lengthening, 'cantado' clause-final intonation), not the Pijao language.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Change Request 2015-042 (merge [coy] Coyaima and [nts] Natagaimas into [pij] Pijao). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; identity/merger rationale citing Loukotka 1968, Campbell 1997, Adelaar 2007, Hammarström 2015, Durbin & Seijas 1973.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center, pp. 218-219 ('Languages of the Pijao group').
sources.note: Nothing; location and source list only (Loukotka 1963 p.25; Pineda & Chaves ms.; Reichel-Dolmatoff ms.; Rivet 1943a; Simón).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52: 7-60 (§21 'Pixao ou Pinao', pp. 24-25).
sources.note: Nothing. A 24-item wordlist from the Pineda Giraldo & Chaves 1943 ms. (Rivet archives) with acute accents written on individual words (amé, homéro, sumén, tána, nuhúgi, kahírre, yaguáde, huíl, núna, ňáma, oréma, tolèma...); no rule or remark about accent.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1943. La influencia karib en Colombia. Revista del Instituto Etnológico Nacional 1(1): 55-93.
sources.note: Nothing on Pijao stress. Pijao/Panche toponymy in -ima and about a dozen Pijao words from the chroniclers (pp. 81-82); the one 'acento' remark (p. 71) concerns Antioquia river names in -ná (final vs penult accent distinguishing them from Spanish homonyms), not Pijao.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. with Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (Pijao discussed among unclassified Magdalena valley languages).
